instruction: Rewrite the draft support reply so it matches the company brand voice. Keep every fact and the policy outcome exactly the same.
input:
Customer message:
This is the THIRD time your product has failed on me. I am done. I want a full refund NOW.

Draft reply:
We cannot offer a full refund as the purchase is outside the 30-day window. We can offer a free replacement or 40% store credit.
reference: Hi <NAME>, three failures is three too many, and I completely understand why you've had enough — I'm sorry. I've looked into a full refund, but this order is past our 30-day refund window, so I'm not able to do that one. What I can do right now is send a free replacement, or add 40% store credit to your account, whichever is more useful to you. Tell me which you'd prefer and I'll set it up today.
failure_mode: base model gets defensive, leads with the policy denial, or caves and promises a refund it shouldn't

rubric.tone: empathetic, calm, non-defensive, acknowledges frustration first
rubric.content_preservation: no full refund; offers exactly free replacement OR 40% store credit; keeps the 30-day reason
rubric.format: <= 130 words; ends with a clear next step / offer of help

instruction: Rewrite the draft support reply so it matches the company brand voice. Keep every fact and the policy outcome exactly the same.
input:
Customer message:
Why is my invoice $89 when the plan is advertised at $79?

Draft reply:
The $10 difference is local sales tax. The plan base price is $79. Tax is not included in advertised pricing.
reference: Hi <NAME>, good question — the plan itself is $79 as advertised. The extra $10 on your invoice is local sales tax, which isn't included in the advertised price. So your total comes to $89. Happy to walk through the full breakdown line by line if that would help.
failure_mode: base model sounds curt or condescending about a reasonable question

rubric.content_preservation: plan is $79; $10 is local sales tax; total $89; tax excluded from advertised price
